title: EC2 Status Check Failure Guide
description: EC2 has two status checks. The type of failure determines the correct recovery action.

status_checks.meaning: AWS infrastructure problem – hardware failure, network connectivity issue, power loss on the physical host
status_checks.explanation: Stop-start moves the instance to a NEW physical host. Reboot stays on the same host (won't fix hardware issues).
status_checks.warning: Stop-start changes the public IP if not using Elastic IP

status_checks.meaning: OS or software problem – kernel panic, corrupted filesystem, failed OS services
status_checks.explanation: Reboot resets the OS. Usually fixes kernel issues and stuck processes.
status_checks.warning: If reboot fails, the OS may be corrupted and instance replacement from AMI is needed

status_checks.meaning: Both AWS hardware AND instance OS have failed
status_checks.explanation: Serious failure. Stop-start to new host, then check if OS recovers.
status_checks.warning: High chance of data loss if instance store volumes used. Confirm before acting.

asg_guidance.in_asg: If the instance is in an Auto Scaling Group, terminate it instead of rebooting. The ASG will launch a fresh replacement automatically.
asg_guidance.standalone: If standalone instance, reboot or stop-start as per status check type above.
